newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU millers want higher wheat flour export refund.
newsitem.headline: EU millers want higher wheat flour export refund.

text.p: The European Union is facing pressure from European millers to step up the daily refund on exports of wheat flour this week after failing to do so last Thursday.
Last week the EU kept the refund on wheat flour exports at 27 Ecus per tonne although it raised the rebate applying to soft wheat exports to 22.35 Ecus from 19.98.
The flour rebate is usually linked to the wheat rebate. To reach a flour rebate, the wheat figure is usually multiplied by a coefficient of 1.37.
Millers, anxious to step up exports, calculated that last week's flour rebate should have been 30.62 Ecus if the 1.37 coefficient had applied.

"European millers have voiced strong criticism with the Commission as its attitude could hurt confidence in the management of the flour market," an official from the European millers' association Euroflour told Reuters.
In a letter to the Commission Euroflour wrote that "to avoid a breach in confidence... we are asking for a strict implementation of the 1.37 coefficent rule."
Millers, who say EU flour exports are sharply behind last year's, want the EU's grain management panel to adjust the wheat flour refund at its weekly meeting on Thursday.
Euroflour said demand for licences to export EU wheat flour currently stodd at 1.1 million tonnes against 1.4 million at the same time last year. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432.
